thing.text:
THE RESORT TEACHER

Everything is out the back
door: the cottages, the
guests, the teacher at the
table.

Go outside.

thing.note: The resort’s own machinery, which you never need to touch: six behaviours, one per guest, three robots each. SPACE here is the six guests arriving at once — they write to the post and walk to their cottages as soon as a clerk answers. Nothing in them knows how many guests there are.
Guest 1’s own three robots: ask the desk where to live, walk to the cottage it is given, and ask again when the bell rings. They work on guest 1, and on nothing else.

active.name: Ask for a place

team.name: Move on the bell I kept
team.note: The bell rang before I had a place, and the pad was kept in hole 7. Now that I have one: the same as Move when told to, on the kept pad.

team.name: Move when told to
team.note: A pad has landed on my nest: the bell, rung for every guest. Sends [where I live, my own bird] to the moving office and takes my place out of the box, so that the answer puts a new one in.

team.name: Keep the bell for later
team.note: The bell rang before I had a place (Move when told to did not fit): takes the pad off my nest into hole 7, which uncovers the address under it.

team.name: Stand at my address
team.note: A number has landed on my nest: that is my address. Works out where that cottage stands along the row, remembers it as my place, and walks there.

active.note: Leads. My number is still in the box, so I have nowhere to live: sends [my number, my own bird] to the desk and takes my number out as it goes, so I never ask twice.

active.name: Ring the bell
active.note: Rings once: gives every guest the pad "a move, please", then switches this behaviour off again through the bird on the perch.

thing.text:
THE ROW GOES ON

Eleven cottages stand in a
row, counted from the left,
and a guest given a number
walks to that cottage.

The row does not stop at the
fence: guest 12 would walk
past it, and guest a thousand
a long way past.

Nothing in these robots knows
how many guests there are.
That is the whole of it.

holes.text: Watch. I seat the guests, teach a clerk, ring the bell, teach a mover, and welcome five more.

holes.name: Next address
holes.note: Untrained. The teacher shows it the clerk’s job on the desk: the letter off the post, a copy of its number to its bird.

holes.name: Move up five
holes.note: Untrained. The teacher shows it the mover’s job on the office desk: the letter off the post, five more on its number, the number to its bird.
A pad with a panel: the robot the teacher puts on its panel works there, on the box it puts with it.

thing.note: A team of three that solves Resort Infinity: seats the guests; teaches a little robot the clerk’s job on the desk and puts it to work on a pad’s panel; rings the bell, teaches another the mover’s job (+5) on the office desk and puts that to work too, then welcomes five more. Three robots because a lesson takes a letter off a post, and a thought about a post is what waits for the letter to land. Nothing here is new: a teaching, Dusty, Ruby, a panel and a switch thrown by mail are steps like any other.

thing.text:
THE RESORT TEACHER

A robot that solves Resort
Infinity in front of you.

Give it the thirteen-hole
box and press Start. Then
watch the grass: the guests
write, a clerk is taught,
six walk to their cottages;
the bell rings, a mover is
taught, everybody moves up
five, and five more take
1 to 5.

Set the Speed to 4x: a
resort takes a while at
walking pace.

WHAT IT DOES

1. A switch letter to "the
guests": six letters land
on the post in the desk.
2. Teaches the first little
robot on the desk: take the
letter, copy the number,
give the copy to the bird,
Dusty, Ruby.
3. Desk and clerk onto the
front desk pad’s panel, and
a switch letter to the pad.
4. A switch letter to the
bell: everybody asks the
office where to move.
5. Teaches the second on the
office desk: the same, with
+5 dropped on the number.
6. Onto the moving office
pad’s panel; switched on.
7. A switch letter to "five
more guests".

WHY A PANEL, AND WHY THREE

One robot works at the
bench, and the teacher is
standing there. A pad’s
panel is a bench of its own:
a box and a robot put on it
work there once the pad is
switched on, and a switch is
thrown by mail, [set |
switch | on] given to a bird
to the pad.

Three robots, because a
lesson takes a letter off a
post and letters take a
moment to fly: a thought
about a post waits for one.

The little robots it taught
stay among its things: click
one with an empty claw to
pick it up and read what it
learned.
